prompt: Make Counter safe for many threads to increment at once, then write ParallelRunner.runConcurrently so it starts the requested number of threads, joins every one of them, and returns the exact final count.
explanation: count++ is a read-modify-write, so two threads can read the same value and each write back the same result, silently losing an increment. Marking increment() and get() synchronized, or holding the value in an AtomicInteger, makes each update indivisible so the total is exact even at 200000 increments. In runConcurrently the second loop is the important one: start() only launches a thread, and without join() the method would return while workers were still counting, giving a different answer every run. Collecting the Thread objects in a list is what lets you start them all first and only then wait for them.
hints: The smallest safe Counter is `private final AtomicInteger count = new AtomicInteger(0);` with increment() calling count.incrementAndGet(). Marking both methods synchronized around a plain int works too.
Build each worker as `new Thread(() -> { for (int n = 0; n < incrementsEach; n++) counter.increment(); })` -- the lambda is the Runnable.
Use two separate loops: the first creates, stores and start()s every thread; the second walks the stored list and calls join() on each. Starting and joining in one loop would run them one at a time.
